wp: WP8 Docs, README, COMPATIBILITY, public e2e
summary: Design for the documentation and public acceptance layer of the single-node serverless work: six new docs/self-hosting pages (install, setup, domains, sleep, branching, upgrade) plus a rewritten overview and docs.json nav; a README rewrite outline that leads with the VPS story while keeping the laptop (local mode) quick start; new and changed COMPATIBILITY.md rows for every route the daemon starts answering (tokens, login --api-key, templates, always-on, limits, compute/domain, multiple services per type, db url/connect through the router) and the ones that stay 501; a CONTRIBUTING code-map update; and an e2e/ directory with two POSIX-sh scripts (local-smoke.sh for local mode on an ubuntu runner with real Docker; server-smoke.sh that runs install.sh on the runner VM itself with self-signed TLS and a loopback sslip.io domain), a shared lib.sh, a tiny fixture template, and a .github/workflows/e2e.yml that runs them as separate jobs so Docker container names never collide. The install-in-a-fresh-Ubuntu-container variant (DinD plus loop mounts) is judged feasible but fragile and is deferred; the runner VM is itself a fresh Ubuntu per job, which is what the server smoke needs. Every 'today' claim and every cloud route is cited by file:line; shared-surface needs on other packages (config knobs for short idle windows, a stable CA file for self-signed TLS, a fork-method field on the branch.created event, a sleeping runtime vocabulary, the setup/sign-up path) are listed for the reconciler.

files.change: Rewrite. Today it is a 29-line page whose body is the laptop quick start (docs/self-hosting/overview.mdx:8-23) and a Note saying 'Full self-hosting documentation is coming soon' (overview.mdx:27-29). New body: what you get on one machine (same CLI, MCP, skills, URL shape, sleep rules, templates, dashboard), the two run modes (server on a VPS behind TLS with auth; local on a laptop with no auth, loopback hostnames, as today), a 'choose a mode' table, and links to the six pages. No em dashes.

New. The one-line VPS install: requirements (root, Linux, Ubuntu 22.04+/Debian 12+, amd64/arm64, 2 vCPU/2 GiB, ports 80/443/5432 free), the exact command, what the script does step by step (Docker install, /var/lib/instacloud, reflink probe and XFS loop image, public IP and sslip.io auto domain, compose.yml + instad.env, up, prints setup URL and 'rerun to upgrade'), every env knob install.sh honours (INSTA_OSS_DOMAIN, INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR, INSTA_OSS_TLS=acme|selfsigned, INSTA_OSS_IMAGE, INSTA_OSS_ACME_EMAIL, idle knobs pass-through), the security posture sentence (the daemon holds the Docker socket, which is root on the box), and a 'local mode on a laptop' section that is today's README quick start (README.md:54-75) verbatim in spirit, with the data dir default ~/.insta-oss.

New. First visit: https://console.<domain>/setup creates the single admin (email + password, hashed in state); dashboard session cookie; the Tokens page mints insta_ keys through the cloud's /tokens routes; the exact `insta login --api-key <k> --api-url https://api.<domain>` line (insta-cli/src/commands/auth.ts:19-24, 80-87); MCP works with the same bearer; every route except /healthz, setup, and static files requires a session or bearer; local mode keeps /me = local with no login (COMPATIBILITY.md:32 today). Includes the headless recipe (curl the sign-up and /tokens routes) the e2e uses.

New. Hostname shape <service>-<project>-<branch>.<domain> with the frozen ref slug (src/engine.ts:45-48), api./console./<bucket>.s3.<domain>; auto domain <ip-with-dashes>.sslip.io and its certificate rate-limit caveat; TLS edge with on-demand per-host certs and self-signed fallback (and where the local CA lives so curl/psql/CLI can trust it); custom domains via `insta compute domain add|status|remove` (insta-cli/src/commands/compute.ts:288-315) backed by the cloud's /projects/:id/compute/domain routes (insta-platform src/server.ts:2781-2806, schema hidden); database and managed-db lanes on 5432/6379/27017 with SNI, MySQL in-network only; local mode: *.localhost names on one router port and how *.localhost resolves (systemd-resolved yes, macOS and Docker containers no, with the /etc/hosts fallback).

New. The idle rules copied from the cloud's sleep-and-wake.md 1.2 to 1.5 (insta-compute docs/sleep-and-wake.md:23-45 stamp writers, :47-68 sweep conditions, :101-119 wake doors and 'a stopped service is never woken by traffic'), the self-host defaults (5 min compute, 10 min databases, sweep 30 s, create grace 10 min, RAM floor 15 percent), memory-pressure eviction of the least-recently-active non-always-on service, sleep = docker stop with a 10 s SIGTERM grace (never pause as primary; today suspend is docker pause, src/adapters/compute.ts:59-61), what wakes (request on any lane, `insta compute start`, deploy), always-on from the manifest or `insta compute always-on on` (insta-cli index.ts:240), limits via `insta compute limits --memory` mapped to --cpus/--memory, the knob table (INSTA_OSS_IDLE_COMPUTE_SEC, INSTA_OSS_IDLE_DB_SEC, INSTA_OSS_SWEEP_SEC, INSTA_OSS_CREATE_GRACE_SEC, INSTA_OSS_MEM_FLOOR_PCT), and the known gap (a long local computation with no traffic sleeps; always-on is the override). States the one deliberate divergence: on self-host a new compute service defaults to scale-to-zero, while the cloud's default for new compute services is always-on (openapi.yaml:6030-6033).

New (self-host specifics only; docs/postgres/branching.mdx stays the product page). Data layout under the data dir (pg/<ref>, vol/<ref>/<group>), clone = CHECKPOINT then reflink copy (cp --reflink=always on XFS/btrfs, cp -c on APFS), pg_basebackup fallback when the probe fails and how to tell which ran (branch.created event payload), volumes fork the same way, buckets stay rclone sync (src/adapters/garage.ts:173-175), a new branch sleeps immediately unless always-on, and the today-vs-target sentence (today pg_dump into memory then psql, src/adapters/postgres.ts:28-31; branch volume empty, src/engine.ts:216-218).

New. Re-run the install one-liner (pulls the pinned image, recreates compose services, state and data untouched under /var/lib/instacloud), pinning INSTA_OSS_VERSION, rollback by rerunning with the previous version, what a restart does to sleeping services (nothing; they stay on disk), backup advice until M7 ships (pg_dump per branch with `insta db url`, tar of vol/, the Garage volumes), and local mode upgrade (git pull, npm install, restart).

Self-hosting group (docs/docs.json:102-106) lists self-hosting/overview, install, setup, domains, sleep, branching, upgrade in that order. CONTRIBUTING.md:78 says a page missing from docs.json builds but is hidden, so every new page is listed.

Rewrite per the outline in the algorithm: VPS story first (one-line install, setup URL, deploy a template, branch, sleep), then local mode quick start (README.md:54-75 today), the example session updated to the new URL shape (README.md:86-94 today prints http://localhost:80 and host port +1000), 'How it works' gains router and scheduler, Dashboard section gains setup/login/tokens/deploy/templates, Templates section notes the daemon serves the bundled catalog, Cleanup section updated for the data dir and compose stack. The single em dash in README.md today is removed.

Rows added or changed as listed in the algorithm section 4 (login --api-key, tokens, services add multiple per type, compute limits/always-on, compute domain, template list/info/deploy, db url/connect, compute start/stop/suspend semantics, branch create = file fork, deploy source mode caveat, backups still 501). MCP table: domain_* moves from the not_supported row to the supported row.

Code map (CONTRIBUTING.md:26-47) gains src/config.ts, src/auth.ts, src/router/, src/scheduler.ts, src/templates.ts, e2e/ (public smoke suite, Docker, integrator-only), test/docs-lint.test.ts. Guidelines gain: 'Docker integration tests and e2e scripts share container names; never run two at once' and 'no em dashes in docs copy'.

New. How to run local-smoke.sh on a laptop and server-smoke.sh on a throwaway VPS, the env knobs, the relationship to the private insta-e2e suite (this is the self-host leg; cleanroom.sh/branch-e2e.sh keep the cloud-only steps and will run this directory as a job).

New. POSIX sh helpers shared by both scripts: FAIL/OK, api() curl wrapper with bearer, jsel() node one-liner (copied from insta-e2e cleanroom.sh:261-264), wait_for(), container_state(), ensure_host() (/etc/hosts fallback), psql_roundtrip(), s3_roundtrip() (cleanroom.sh:83-115 logic without the io-garage rewrite), url_host(), measure().
New. Local-mode smoke, steps in algorithm section 6.
New. Server-mode smoke that runs install.sh on the runner VM, steps in algorithm section 7.

New. A minimal manifest for the template-deploy step: code tpl-hello, version 0.1.0, maintainer official, upstream pinned, one web service on image traefik/whoami:v1.10 port 80 healthcheck /, env.fixed WHOAMI_NAME, env.generated HELLO_TOKEN from a declared generator secret:32, meta.draft: true so templates lint and publish ignore it (templates/AGENTS.md:100-101), and it lives under e2e/ not templates/ so the catalog never lists it.
New workflow, jobs local and server (algorithm section 8). ci.yml (unit + Docker integration tests, .github/workflows/ci.yml:9-20) is unchanged.

New fake-adapter-free unit test: no U+2014 in README.md, COMPATIBILITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/**/*.mdx, e2e/**; every docs/**/*.mdx path appears in docs.json; `sh -n` passes on e2e/*.sh; e2e/fixtures/tpl-hello manifest pins its image and declares draft.

sharedSurface.types: WP8 adds no fields to src/types.ts or src/state.ts. It DEPENDS on these additions from other packages and the reconciler should confirm the names: (1) AuditEvent payload of kind 'branch.created' carries { from, method: 'reflink' | 'basebackup', ms } (branching WP) so docs and e2e can name which fork ran; (2) AuditEvent kinds 'service.sleep' { service, reason: 'idle' | 'memory' } and 'service.wake' { service, door: 'http' | 'tcp' | 'start' | 'deploy' } (scheduler/router WP) for the sleep page and the e2e event assertions; (3) the runtime vocabulary on GET /projects/:id/services (`runtime`), GET .../services/:sid/state (`state`) and /runtime-health distinguishes an asleep service ('sleeping' / 'standby') from a crashed one; today runtimeHealth maps exited-against-running-intent to 'crashed' (src/engine.ts:733-737) and services() maps any non-running container to 'stopped' (src/engine.ts:431-432); (4) Branch.apps[group].alwaysOn?: boolean and .limits?: { cpu, memoryMb } (scheduler WP) read back by GET .../limits and shown in docs; (5) a config module src/config.ts exporting the resolved knobs below.
sharedSurface.config: Knobs the docs describe and the e2e sets; owner in parentheses, WP8 only reads them. INSTA_OSS_MODE=local|server (config WP; default local when unset, server inside the image). INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR (host path; default ~/.insta-oss local, /var/lib/instacloud server). INSTA_OSS_STATE (exists today, src/state.ts:17; docs say it defaults under the data dir). INSTA_OSS_PORT (exists, src/main.ts:12-13). INSTA_OSS_ROUTER_PORT (router WP; local mode single router port, default = API port or 8090, open question). INSTA_OSS_DOMAIN (router WP; 'localhost' in local mode, <ip-dashes>.sslip.io written by install.sh in server mode). INSTA_OSS_TLS=acme|selfsigned and INSTA_OSS_ACME_EMAIL (install/edge WP; the e2e needs selfsigned because ACME cannot reach a GitHub runner). INSTA_OSS_CA_FILE default <data dir>/edge/ca.pem (install/edge WP; ONE local CA that signs every self-signed per-host cert so curl --cacert, psql PGSSLROOTCERT and NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS can trust the box; without it the e2e falls back to -k and NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0). INSTA_OSS_IMAGE and INSTA_OSS_VERSION (install WP; the server smoke builds the image from the checkout and passes it so install.sh skips the pull). INSTA_OSS_IDLE_COMPUTE_SEC (default 300), INSTA_OSS_IDLE_DB_SEC (600), INSTA_OSS_SWEEP_SEC (30), INSTA_OSS_CREATE_GRACE_SEC (600), INSTA_OSS_MEM_FLOOR_PCT (15), INSTA_OSS_MEM_BUDGET_MB (optional synthetic total for eviction accounting so a test can force eviction) (scheduler WP; install.sh must pass any of these it finds in its environment into instad.env). INSTA_OSS_MAX_SERVICES_PER_TYPE (project-parity WP; cloud free tier is 5, pro 25, team/enterprise 100 per type per branch, insta-platform src/config.ts:469-474; docs state the self-host default and that it is a per-install setting). INSTA_OSS_S3_HOST_ENDPOINT and INSTA_OSS_GARAGE_CONFIG exist today (src/adapters/garage.ts:25, 202) and the docs say they are superseded by the data dir and domain.
sharedSurface.engineSeams: None added by WP8. Read-only seams the e2e relies on and the docs describe (owners in parentheses): Engine.createBranch emits branch.created with the fork method (branching WP); the scheduler exposes sleep/wake through existing routes only: POST .../services/:sid/start|stop (src/server.ts:323-330) where stop sets the durable 'stopped' intent that traffic never wakes and start clears it; GET .../services/:sid/state; PUT .../always-on and GET/PUT .../limits replace the 501s at src/server.ts:503-505; POST /projects/:id/template-deployments + GET /template-deployments/:id (templates WP) return the cloud's TemplateDeployment shape so `insta template deploy` polls unchanged (insta-cli/src/commands/template.ts:400-417); POST /orgs/:id/projects returns resources: [] and provisions nothing (project-parity WP; today src/server.ts:142-156 returns the postgres/storage/compute trio and src/engine.ts:107-126 provisions main with db + storage). The e2e never calls engine methods; it drives the CLI and curl.

algorithm:
SECTION 1. Docs pages: exact outlines (Mintlify mdx, frontmatter title + description; prose uses commas, colons and periods, never an em dash; code blocks are copy-pasteable; every claim about behaviour names the CLI command that shows it).

1.1 docs/self-hosting/overview.mdx
- H2 'What you get': one daemon over Docker that serves the cloud's API; same insta CLI, MCP server and skills; same URL shape per service; same sleep rules; same templates catalog served from the repo; the dashboard. One sentence on what is not there: billing, orgs, members, multi-node, backups until a later milestone (link to upgrade page).
- H2 'Two ways to run' table: columns Mode / Where / Address / Auth / Data dir / Use it for. Rows: server (a VPS, https://api.<domain> and https://console.<domain>, admin account + insta_ tokens, /var/lib/instacloud, production and shared use) and local (your laptop, http://127.0.0.1:8080 and *.localhost service names, none, ~/.insta-oss, development and CI).
- H2 'Next': links to install, setup, domains, sleep, branching, upgrade.

1.2 docs/self-hosting/install.mdx
- H2 'Requirements': root, Linux (Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+), amd64 or arm64, 2 vCPU and 2 GiB minimum, ports 80, 443 and 5432 free (the script refuses otherwise), outbound HTTPS. Docker is installed if missing.
- H2 'Install': `curl -fsSL https://get.instacloud.com | sh`. Then a numbered list of what it does (mirrors spec section 1 items 1 to 5) and the two lines it prints: the setup URL and the upgrade note.
- H2 'What the script writes': /var/lib/instacloud tree (compose.yml, instad.env, state.json, pg/, vol/, garage/, edge/ with ca.pem when self-signed, data.img when the loop image was needed) and an fstab line for the loop mount.
- H2 'Options' table of environment variables read by install.sh: INSTA_OSS_DOMAIN (default <ip-with-dashes>.sslip.io), INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR, INSTA_OSS_TLS (acme default, selfsigned for air-gapped or CI), INSTA_OSS_ACME_EMAIL, INSTA_OSS_VERSION, INSTA_OSS_IMAGE (a prebuilt local image, skips the pull), idle knobs (link to sleep page). Example: `INSTA_OSS_DOMAIN=cloud.example.com curl -fsSL https://get.instacloud.com | sh` with a note that a real domain needs a wildcard A record pointing at the box.
- H2 'Reflinks' : why (branch forks in constant time), the probe, the XFS loop image on ext4, native on btrfs/ZFS/XFS-with-reflink, how to check (`xfs_info /var/lib/instacloud | grep reflink=1`).
- H2 'Security posture': the daemon container mounts the Docker socket, which is root on the box; treat the admin password and every insta_ token as root credentials; put the box behind your provider firewall except 80, 443 and the database ports you use.
- H2 'Local mode on a laptop': Docker running, Node 22+, `git clone`, `npm install`, `npm run build:ui`, `npm run dev`; state under ~/.insta-oss (or INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR); `export INSTA_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080`; no login; service URLs are http://<service>-<project>-<branch>.localhost:<router port>; the note that Docker containers and macOS do not resolve *.localhost on their own and the /etc/hosts line to add. This replaces the text at docs/self-hosting/overview.mdx:8-23 today.

1.3 docs/self-hosting/setup.mdx
- H2 'First visit': open https://console.<domain>/setup, enter email and password, one admin in v1, stored hashed in state (scrypt), the page then signs you in.
- H2 'Sign in later': https://console.<domain>/login; sessions are httpOnly cookies.
- H2 'CLI and agents': Tokens page, create token, copy the exact line `insta login --api-key insta_... --api-url https://api.<domain>`; explains that --api-key is verified against GET /me (insta-cli/src/commands/auth.ts:98-108) and that a token must start with insta_; INSTA_API_URL alternative and the config precedence (insta-cli/src/config.ts:28-35); a switch back to the cloud is `insta env use prod` or unsetting INSTA_API_URL (config.ts:50-56 scrubs a foreign session).
- H2 'MCP': same bearer via the insta-mcp server's PLATFORM_API_URL=https://api.<domain> (README.md:141-142 today shows the localhost form).
- H2 'Headless setup' (what CI does): three curl commands: sign-up (POST /api/auth/sign-up/email with a cookie jar), mint (POST /tokens {name}) and login. Note that sign-up is refused once an admin exists.
- H2 'What requires auth': everything except /healthz, /setup, /login and static files; local mode keeps today's behaviour (`user: local`, COMPATIBILITY.md:14).

1.4 docs/self-hosting/domains.mdx
- H2 'Hostnames': table service type -> example: compute web on project shop branch main -> https://web-shop-main.<domain>; postgres db -> db-shop-main.<domain>:5432; redis cache -> cache-shop-main.<domain>:6379; api.<domain>; console.<domain>; public bucket <bucket>.s3.<domain>. Ref = <project>-<branch> frozen at creation (a rename never changes it, src/engine.ts:39-48), so URLs survive renames.
- H2 'Auto domain': sslip.io of the public IP; per-host certificates; the auto domain shares certificate rate limits with everyone using it, so production wants a real domain.
- H2 'Your own domain': set INSTA_OSS_DOMAIN at install (wildcard A record) or add a custom domain to one service: `insta compute domain add web shop.example.com`, point a CNAME at web-shop-main.<domain>, `insta compute domain status web shop.example.com`, `insta compute domain remove ...`; the edge issues on first request.
- H2 'TLS': the edge issues on demand; self-signed fallback and INSTA_OSS_TLS=selfsigned write a local CA to <data dir>/edge/ca.pem; how to trust it: `curl --cacert`, `PGSSLROOTCERT`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` for the CLI.
- H2 'Databases from anywhere': `psql "$(insta db url)"` and `insta db connect` work from your laptop because 5432 is proxied by SNI (libpq sends SNI since Postgres 14; use sslmode=require); redis and mongo the same on 6379 and 27017; MySQL has no SNI, so it is reachable inside the branch network only (in-network lane) in v1.
- H2 'Inside a branch': apps reach databases through the same names; the router sits on every branch network, so a sleeping database wakes when the app connects.
- H2 'Local mode': names end in .localhost on one router port, resolution notes (systemd-resolved resolves *.localhost, macOS and containers need /etc/hosts or curl --resolve), no TLS.

1.5 docs/self-hosting/sleep.mdx
- H2 'The promise': dozens of branches on one box, only the active ones use RAM.
- H2 'What counts as activity': the activity stamp rules verbatim from the cloud doc (request start and every 5 s while a handler runs on the HTTP lane; every non-empty read on a database connection; a silent open connection holds one window only; outbound traffic, CPU and disk never count).
- H2 'When a service sleeps': the five sweep conditions (running, not always-on, stamp older than the window, older than the create grace, no operation in flight), cadence 30 s, defaults 5 min compute and 10 min databases, so a service sleeps 5 to 5.5 minutes after its last request.
- H2 'Memory pressure': eviction of the least recently active non-always-on service when free RAM drops below the floor (15 percent) or a wake needs room; always-on services are never evicted.
- H2 'What sleep does': docker stop, SIGTERM, 10 s grace; disk survives; Postgres does a fast shutdown and comes back in 1 to 3 s; redis appendonly, mysql and mongo shut down cleanly.
- H2 'What wakes a service': a request or connection on any lane (held until ready, at most 60 s), `insta compute start`, a deploy. A service you stopped with `insta compute stop` is never woken by traffic; start it again explicitly.
- H2 'Always-on and limits': `insta compute always-on on web`, `services add compute --always-on`, manifest alwaysOn: true (hermes, n8n, openclaw declare it, templates/hermes/insta.template.yaml:24); `insta compute limits web --memory 512mb` maps to --memory and --cpus and feeds the eviction budget. The divergence note: the self-host default for a new compute service is scale-to-zero; the cloud's default is always-on (openapi.yaml:6030).
- H2 'Tuning' table of the knobs and where to set them (instad.env, then `docker compose up -d`).
- H2 'Known edge': a long computation with no inbound traffic looks idle; always-on is the override.

Docker integration tests (integrator only, sequential): test/sleep.int.test.ts (new, scheduler WP) asserts docker stop not pause and wake on connect with 2 s windows; test/fork.int.test.ts (new, branching WP) asserts reflink when available and basebackup fallback otherwise; existing clone-isolation.int.test.ts, storage.int.test.ts, restart.int.test.ts keep passing.

e2e/local-smoke.sh on ubuntu-latest with real Docker (job local): every step in algorithm section 6; hard assertions are the container states, the URL shape, the round trips, the isolation, the volume fork marker, the empty project start, and the teardown sweep; soft (OK-skip) assertions are branch timing, fork method, always-on, limits, second-copy naming, sleep/wake event kinds.

e2e/server-smoke.sh on ubuntu-latest (job server): every step in algorithm section 7; hard assertions add the XFS reflink mount, 401 without auth, sign-up once, insta_ token mint, --api-key login, https URL shape, psql over public 5432 with SNI, reflink fork method, upgrade idempotence.

Not tested in CI (documented): ACME issuance on a public IP, the sslip.io auto domain on a real public IP, custom domain DNS and certificates, memory-pressure eviction under real RAM pressure (only via the synthetic INSTA_OSS_MEM_BUDGET_MB knob if the scheduler WP adds it; otherwise the eviction step is absent), `insta db connect` interactivity, arm64.
risks: *.localhost resolution: systemd-resolved on the runner answers 127.0.0.1 for any *.localhost name, but Docker containers, macOS and glibc-without-resolved do not; the local smoke therefore runs on the host and carries an /etc/hosts fallback (ensure_host). The private suite's node:20-container pattern (insta-e2e run.sh, e2e.yml:32-34) cannot host the self-host leg any more.

sslip.io is a third-party DNS dependency for the server smoke (127-0-0-1.sslip.io); an outage fails the job. Mitigated by the same /etc/hosts fallback for api., console. and every service host the script touches.

Self-signed TLS trust: if the edge issues independent self-signed certs per host with no shared CA, curl/psql/Node cannot trust the box and the e2e degrades to -k and NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, which weakens the assertion that the CLI works against a self-hosted box. Listed as a shared-surface requirement (INSTA_OSS_CA_FILE).

Sleep timing flakiness: the e2e depends on short idle knobs (15 s / 20 s, sweep 2 s, grace 0). If the scheduler WP does not expose them, or install.sh does not pass them into instad.env, the sleep step cannot run in CI time and becomes an OK-skip, leaving the headline feature unproven publicly.
Image pull time and runner disk: postgres, garage, rclone, whoami, plus the daemon image; the workflow pre-pulls and the server job builds the daemon image on the runner (multi-arch not covered).

Container name collisions: e2e and test/*.int.test.ts share io-<ref>-* names and the shared io-garage container (src/adapters/garage.ts:15); running them on one machine at once corrupts both. The workflow isolates them by job; the CONTRIBUTING rule makes it explicit for humans.

Hostname form for multiple postgres services: the spec's examples say pg-<ref> (spec section 3) while decision 4 says <service>-<ref>; with several postgres per project the service name must be in the host. The docs and e2e read hostnames from CLI output instead of computing them, but the domains page has to print one form; it is written for <service>-<ref> and flagged.

Cloud default for new compute services is always-on (openapi.yaml:6030-6033, insta-cli index.ts:138) while the self-host default per decision 3 is sleep; the sleep page documents the divergence, but users porting `services add compute --no-always-on` scripts will see no difference locally, and `--always-on` must be honoured or the docs are wrong.

Docs drift: docs/postgres/branching.mdx:14-19 already promises copy-on-write and empty volumes on the cloud; the self-host branching page must not contradict the product page (volumes fork on self-host, stay empty on the cloud), so both pages state the difference explicitly.
Em dash sweep: README.md carries one today and the private suite's shell output uses them; the docs-lint test covers only files in this repo.
openQuestions: Postgres and managed-db hostname form with several services per type: <service>-<ref>.<domain> (decision 4) or pg-<ref> (spec examples)? The domains page and the server smoke regex need one answer.

Local mode database lane: how does the router pick the branch on one port without TLS? SNI over a self-signed TLS handshake (libpq sslmode=prefer sends SNI; node pg does not by default) or a port per database service? The e2e uses the printed DSN with psql and works either way, but the domains page has to explain it.
Does local mode put the router on the API port (Host-based split: api at 127.0.0.1, services at *.localhost) or on INSTA_OSS_ROUTER_PORT (default 8090)? Affects every URL in the docs.

Setup path: is the setup page's call POST /api/auth/sign-up/email (Better Auth, openapi.yaml:2191, betterauth.ts:152) with the daemon refusing a second sign-up, or a daemon-internal form post? The e2e's headless setup and the setup page docs assume the Better Auth path.
Fork method visibility: will branch.created carry {method, ms} in its payload (needed for the server smoke's hard reflink assertion and the branching page's 'how to tell')?

Runtime vocabulary for an asleep service in GET services (`runtime`), .../state (`state`), and /runtime-health (`status`): 'sleeping', 'standby', or 'stopped'? The sleep page and the compute status assertion print it.
INSTA_OSS_MAX_SERVICES_PER_TYPE default for self-host: 5 (cloud free), 25 (cloud pro), or unlimited? COMPATIBILITY needs the number.
Will install.sh honour INSTA_OSS_IMAGE (skip pull, use a local tag) and INSTA_OSS_TLS=selfsigned with a shared CA file? Both are required for the server smoke to run in GitHub Actions.
Compose service names and the edge product name: the install page and the server smoke's `docker ps` assertion need the exact container names.

Governance section of the README: Tony's FAQ decision (spec FAQ 'What about governance?') decides whether the README keeps the governance paragraph (README.md:34-38) and whether COMPATIBILITY keeps the policy/approvals rows.

Should the public suite also carry the memory-pressure eviction step? It needs a synthetic budget knob (INSTA_OSS_MEM_BUDGET_MB) from the scheduler WP; without it the step is omitted and eviction is Docker-integration-test-only.
